title: DOJ Says Georgia Inmates Ran Fake Jury Duty Scams, 800+ Targeted
summary: Jury duty scam from prison: on November 24, 2026 the Justice Department announced what it called the largest crackdown on scammers in its history — more than 400 cases against more than 800 defendants since March 6 — and singled out a scheme in which, federal officials say, Georgia prison inmates phoned Americans, claimed they had missed jury duty and demanded 'bond' payments at crypto ATMs. This video walks through the scheme using a federal seizure-warrant affidavit (D.N.J. 26-mj-8230), the Justice Department's announcement and its anti-scam surge page: the phone call, the payment, the fake court websites, the contraband phones, and the indictments, sentences, seizures and rules the Justice Department lists. The affidavit and the indictments contain allegations; defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty, and the affidavit charges no one.

question: Have you ever gotten a 'you missed jury duty' call — and should state prisons be allowed to jam phone signals? Tell us in the comments.
first_comment: The affidavit says scammers send bogus documents to convince victims that paying at a crypto ATM is a legitimate form of payment. Have you ever gotten a 'you missed jury duty' call? What did you do?
